newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-HANZLIK NAMED NUGGETS' COACH.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-HANZLIK NAMED NUGGETS' COACH.

text.p: Bill Hanzlik was named the new coach of the restructured Denver Nuggets on Thursday.
The 38-year-old Hanzlik played nine of his 11 seasons with the Nuggets and worked for five years with the Charlotte Hornets as an assistant to Allan Bristow, the club's vice president.
Bristow and his staff were fired by the Hornets after the 1995-96 season, and Hanzlik latched on with the Atlanta Hawks as an assistant under Lenny Wilkens.

"Even after I left to go on what I felt was sort of a sabbatical -- a little learning process in coaching underneath Allan in Charlotte, then with Lenny Wilkens and Dick Helm in Atlanta this past year -- I feel I'm ready," Hanzlik said. "I'm ready and excited."
The move was the second in three days for the Nuggets, who hired Mike D'Antoni as director of player personnel Tuesday.

One day after the Nuggets completed a 21-61 season -- the second-worst mark in franchise history -- Bristow fired coach Dick Motta and his entire staff. Denver has the fifth, 32nd and 40th picks in the draft.
Bristow interviewed Hanzlik for the team's coaching vacancy on May 19th. Previously, he had interviewed former NBA coaches Paul Westphal and John Lucas.

"Bill Hanzlik is a perfect fit for the Denver Nuggets organisation," Bristow said. "He has an outstanding basketball mind, has fantastic rapport with players. He knows the type of basketball the fans in this town want to see and will work tirelessly to help return the Nuggets to glory."

"I think this is a unique situation where all the pieces fit right," Hanzlik said. "A lot of times guys have an opportunity to take a head coaching job, and it's just a head coaching job. Well, to me this is a special head coaching job because I want to be here."
Bristow took over in mid-season after Bernie Bickerstaff took the coaching vacancy of the Washington Bullets. Motta already had replaced Bickerstaff on the sidelines.
